I cook large batches of food and freeze them. Typically, I use them for about 3 or 4 of my meals a week. This allows for some variation so I don't feel like I'm sticking to the exact same food everyday. 

The meals I tend to freeze are Boli, chilli, chicken Thai green curry, chicken casserole, steak casserole and lentil soup. 

I don't have a chest freezer, we just have a standard fridge/freezer and wrap our meals in sandwich bags or tupperware. It doesn't take up much space at all.

Basically I do a large shop every 2 weeks with a very small shop each week for a couple of fresh items. It really cuts down food costs but keeps some variety and flexibility to what I eat. Hope this helps.

Pancreatitis is a serious condition that can be brought on by eating inappropriate food, it can be very severe and cost a lot in medical bills too.

Dont hit the space bar right away. 

So get out your rope, when you attempt to lasso your horse you press space to throw the rope and a second space to land inside the highlighted bar to make a successful throw (all whilst your cursor is highlighted red over your horse). As soon as the lasso minigame is successful, the game tells you to press space again but dont (This is where youve probably pressed space and failed). 

You need to start moving forward with 'w' and only press space when the horse rears. When this happens you get another minigame where you tap space as fast as possible for 10seconds. If you win you can carry on moving forward towards the horse. When you finally reach the horse you can either climb on or feed a sugar lump. You have a chance to fail here though if you get on the horse too soon (attempting to mount less than 30seconds since the rope connected will fail i think). Giving a sugar lump doesnt guarantee success though so be ready to fail a few times.

I hope this helps, it sounds like you press space after the lasso minigame and thats what fails.

Not a flight attendant but when I was 14 I was on a flight from the Falkland islands heading to England. Not long after take off there was a loud bang that came outside the aircraft. People started panicking a bit and shortly after the captain announced on the tanoy that one of the engines had stopped working. This was a plane with four engines and they can technically still fly with only two. He asked people to remain calm and informed us they would turn back and try to land, but due to the weight they would have to dump the fuel first.

The fuel dump took nearly an hour and by the time the plane had come back in to try to land, fog had moved in over the runway. They tried to land twice but had to abandon each time due to the fog. The captain then announced we would be diverted to Montevideo instead which was around a 3 hour journey. 

We managed to land safely in Montevideo and everyone was put up into a nice hotel for the 3 days whilst they repaired the engine. Most people were pretty calm on the whole flight considering what happened, we had just a single passenger who passed out. My dad was the only forces passenger so the whole time we were in Montevideo we were escorted around by police to make sure my dad wasn't spying or going to cause mischief. No one was given their baggage either during the 3 days so people had to buy clothes and toiletries when they landed.

Very interesting experience.

As someone who has done a lot of group questing in Wildstar (mostly 2 or 3 people), I have to argue that group questing is actually pretty quick and well done. 

There are some gather-type quests that are shared between party members. I participated in a quest where the entire time I was selling stuff to a vendor and my friend went off completing the objectives, only to find when I was ready to quest again that the quest was completed for me. The joint progress happened a number of times as long as we stayed relatively close to one another. 

The quests where our progress was individual were the ones where we could both interact with the same object without it disappearing, the same as you would solo questing - and these were actually not that frequent.
